workoutPlans.description: An intelligent 4-day hybrid Push/Pull/Legs/Upper split engineered for maximum mechanical tension, progressive overload, and systematic deloading.

workouts.title: Push Day A — Chest, Delts & Triceps
workouts.focus: Upper Body Pressing & Mid Deltoid Density
warmUp: 5 min dynamic shoulder arm circles & band dislocates
1 warmup set barbell bench with empty bar x 12

exercises.name: Barbell Flat Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on the bench with eyes positioned directly under the barbell.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width, retact and depress shoulder blades.
Unrack the bar and stabilize it directly over mid-chest with elbows extended.
Inhale and lower the bar in a controlled diagonal arc to touch the mid-sternum.
Press explosively through the palms while driving feet into the floor until arms lock out.
safetyNotes: Always keep wrists neutral and directly stacked over elbows.
Do not bounce the bar off your ribcage.
Use safety pins or a spotter when lifting near failure.

alternatives.name: Dumbbell Flat Bench Press
alternatives.reason: Better range of motion and joint-friendly unilateral loading.

alternatives.name: Machine Chest Press
alternatives.reason: Fixed path reduces stabilizer fatigue and maximizes mechanical tension.

alternatives.name: Push-ups
alternatives.reason: No equipment needed; can be elevated or weighted for progressive overload.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 30 to 45-degree angle.
Sit back with dumbbells rested on thighs, kick them up to shoulder level one by one.
Retract your scapulae and keep your lower back slightly arched.
Press dumbbells upward along a natural convergent arc until elbows are almost locked.
Lower under control until you feel a deep stretch in the upper pectorals.
safetyNotes: Avoid setting the bench higher than 45 degrees to avoid shifting emphasis to shoulders.
Do not let dumbbells flare outward past 75 degrees from torso.

alternatives.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
alternatives.reason: Higher absolute load capability.

alternatives.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
alternatives.reason: Continuous tension at peak contraction.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding dumbbells at sides with neutral grip.
Slight forward lean (10 degrees) at hips to align with scapular plane.
Raise dumbbells out to the sides leading with elbows until parallel to the floor.
Brief pause at shoulder height, then lower slowly for a 3-second count.
safetyNotes: Do not swing or use hip thrusting momentum.
Avoid internally rotating hands ("pouring water"), which impinges the rotator cuff.

alternatives.name: Cable Lateral Raise
alternatives.reason: Maintains uniform resistance curve throughout entire arc.

alternatives.name: Resistance Band Lateral Raise
alternatives.reason: Easily adjustable tension.

exercises.name: Cable Tricep Rope Pushdown
instructions: Attach rope attachment to high cable pulley.
Grasp rope, bend elbows 90 degrees with upper arms pinned to your sides.
Extend elbows downward, spreading rope ends apart at the bottom to lock out.
Hold peak squeeze for 1 second, then allow forearms to rise to 90 degrees under control.
safetyNotes: Keep elbows stationary; do not let elbows drift forward and back.

alternatives.name: Overhead Dumbbell Tricep Extension
alternatives.reason: Focuses heavily on the triceps long head.

alternatives.name: Bench Dips
alternatives.reason: Bodyweight tricep builder.

workouts.title: Pull Day A — Lat Width & Spinal Thickness

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit comfortably at the lat pulldown station with thighs secured under roller pads.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with an overhand grip.
Lean back slightly (10-15 degrees) and draw scapulae down before pulling.
Pull the bar down toward upper chest by driving elbows down and back.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then resist the bar as it ascends to a full stretch.
safetyNotes: Never pull behind the neck, which places excessive stress on the cervical spine.
Avoid swinging excessively with momentum.

alternatives.name: Pull-ups
alternatives.reason: Gold standard bodyweight vertical pull.

alternatives.name: Resistance Band Pulldown
alternatives.reason: Can be anchored to a high door or bar.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
instructions: Sit on the bench with knees slightly bent and feet firmly on footrests.
Grasp the V-grip handle and sit upright with spine neutral and shoulders relaxed.
Pull the handle into your lower abdomen while retracting your shoulder blades.
Squeeze your back muscles for 1 full second at peak contraction.
Return smoothly with arms extending and shoulder blades opening into a gentle stretch.
safetyNotes: Keep core braced; do not let your torso rock back and forth significantly.

alternatives.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
alternatives.reason: Unilateral free weight option with deep stretch.

alternatives.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
alternatives.reason: High recruitment of full posterior chain.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
instructions: Attach a rope to cable pulley set around eye level.
Grip rope ends with thumbs pointing backward or overhand.
Step back, pull rope directly toward bridge of nose or forehead.
Externally rotate shoulders at the finish so your knuckles are pointing back and elbows stay high.
Hold the contraction for 2 seconds, then slowly return.
safetyNotes: Keep weight light; this is a posture-restoration and shoulder-health builder.

alternatives.name: Band Pull-Aparts
alternatives.reason: Convenient warm-up and postural accessory anywhere.

alternatives.name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly
alternatives.reason: Free weight isolation of rear delts.

exercises.name: Standing Barbell Bicep Curl
instructions: Stand upright holding bar with shoulder-width underhand (supinated) grip.
Keep elbows pinned closely by your ribcage.
Curl the bar upward toward upper chest by flexing elbows.
Squeeze biceps hard at the peak, then lower in a controlled 3-second descent.
safetyNotes: Do not lean backward or swing with your lower back.
Use an EZ-curl bar if straight bar creates wrist or elbow discomfort.

alternatives.name: Dumbbell Incline Curl
alternatives.reason: Maximizes long head stretch under passive tension.

alternatives.name: Cable Bicep Curl
alternatives.reason: Continuous tension at peak contraction.

workouts.title: Leg Day — Quad & Glute Hypertrophy
workouts.focus: Knee extension, hinge loading & posterior chain

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
instructions: Step under bar resting across upper traps (high bar) or rear delts (low bar).
Unrack, take two controlled steps back into shoulder-width stance, toes angled slightly out.
Take a deep belly breath, brace core 360 degrees.
Break at hips and knees simultaneously, descending until hip crease is below knee cap.
Drive powerfully out of the hole, keeping chest tall and knees tracking over toes.
safetyNotes: Ensure knees do not collapse inward (valgus collapse).
Keep heels glued to the floor; use squat shoes or heel plates if ankle mobility is tight.

alternatives.name: Goblet Squat
alternatives.reason: Superb for beginners learning upright squat posture.

alternatives.name: Leg Press
alternatives.reason: High quad overload with zero spinal loading.

alternatives.name: Bodyweight Squats
alternatives.reason: Fundamentals and high-rep endurance.

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
instructions: Hold barbell at hip level with an overhand grip, knees slightly soft (unlocked).
Hinge hips backward as if touching a wall behind you with your glutes.
Slide the barbell down your thighs while keeping your spine neutral and lats packed.
Descend until you feel a maximum stretch in hamstrings (usually mid-shin).
Contract hamstrings and drive hips forward to return to standing lockout.
safetyNotes: Do not bend knees into a squat; this is a pure hip hinge movement.
Stop descending once your hips stop traveling backward to prevent lower back rounding.

alternatives.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
alternatives.reason: Allows natural arm path closer to body center of mass.

alternatives.name: Lying Leg Curl
alternatives.reason: Direct knee flexion isolation for hamstrings.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Walking Lunges
instructions: Hold dumbbells at sides with arms relaxed and torso upright.
Take a comfortable forward stride and lower your rear knee until it gently hovers above the floor.
Ensure front shin is relatively vertical or tracking over mid-foot.
Push through front heel to rise smoothly into the next forward step.
safetyNotes: Avoid slamming your rear kneecap into the gym floor.
Keep pelvis level to avoid twisting.

alternatives.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
alternatives.reason: Static unilateral exercise with high hypertrophy stimulus.

alternatives.name: Bodyweight Reverse Lunges
alternatives.reason: Kinder on knees and requires no equipment.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
instructions: Position balls of feet on platform with heels hanging off edge.
Lower heels as deep as comfortable into a full 3-second calf stretch.
Press up through the balls of your big toes into maximal ankle plantarflexion.
Hold the top contraction for 2 seconds before descending.
safetyNotes: Do not bounce quickly at the bottom to avoid Achilles tendon irritation.

alternatives.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Calf Raise
alternatives.reason: Unilateral free weight option on a step.

alternatives.name: Seated Calf Raise
alternatives.reason: Emphasizes soleus muscle with bent knees.

workouts.title: Upper Body Density & Weak Point Overload

exercises.name: Standing Barbell Overhead Press
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, gripping bar just outside your shoulders.
Rest bar across upper clavicles, squeeze glutes, brace abs, and tighten quads.
Tilt head slightly back to clear chin and press the bar straight up.
Once bar passes forehead, push head slightly forward to lock bar directly over crown.
Lower under control back to clavicle shelf.
safetyNotes: Do not lean backward excessively to turn the lift into an incline bench press.
Keep your glutes locked to protect the lumbar spine.

alternatives.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
alternatives.reason: Reduced balance demand and independent arm control.

alternatives.name: Pike Push-ups
alternatives.reason: No equipment needed vertical pressing pattern.

exercises.name: Cable Chest Fly
instructions: Set cable pulleys at chest height with D-handles attached.
Step forward into a staggered stance to stabilize your core.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Bring handles together in front of your chest in a hugging motion, squeezing hard for 1s.
Control the eccentric return until you feel a mild stretch.
safetyNotes: Do not overstretch shoulders behind torso plane if you have anterior shoulder instability.

alternatives.name: Dumbbell Flys
alternatives.reason: Free weight alternative with stretch focus.

alternatives.name: Resistance Band Chest Fly
alternatives.reason: Home gym setup without pulleys.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells with palms facing each other (neutral grip).
Curl dumbbells simultaneously or alternating, keeping elbows tucked.
Hold at the top for 1 second, then lower steadily.
safetyNotes: Keep shoulders back and chest open.

alternatives.name: Rope Cable Hammer Curl
alternatives.reason: Constant resistance through elbow flexion.

alternatives.name: Resistance Band Hammer Curl
alternatives.reason: Portable high-rep finisher.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Lying Triceps Extension (Skull Crushers)
instructions: Lie on flat bench with EZ-bar held directly above forehead with overhand grip.
Angle upper arms slightly back toward your head (10 degrees) to keep tension on triceps.
Hinge strictly at elbows to lower the bar toward the crown of your head.
Contract triceps to extend arms back to the starting position.
safetyNotes: Use a controlled descent to protect your forehead and elbows.
Warm up elbows thoroughly before heavy sets.

alternatives.name: Dumbbell Skull Crushers
alternatives.reason: Allows natural wrist rotation without joint strain.

alternatives.name: Diamond Push-ups
alternatives.reason: Bodyweight tricep extension movement.

exercises.name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell crossing directly over mid-foot.
Hinge at hips to grab the bar just outside your knees with double-overhand or hook grip.
Pull your chest proud, engage your lats ("pack your armpits"), and wedge your hips.
Drive the floor away through mid-foot while keeping the bar in contact with shins.
Lock out hips and knees simultaneously without hyperextending your lumbar spine.
safetyNotes: Never allow the lower back to round into flexion under heavy loading.
Reset your breath and brace using the Valsalva maneuver before every single rep.

Keep chin tucked and ribs down to prevent lumbar hyperextension.
Squeeze glutes maximally for a full 2-second hold at the top before lowering.
safetyNotes: Always use a bar pad to protect pelvic crests.
Keep eyes forward looking at your knees at lockout to maintain posterior pelvic tilt.

Lower under complete control without letting momentum take over.

Pull with your abs and lats to roll back into starting position.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Russian Swing
instructions: Stand feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell 1 foot in front of you.
Hinge back and hike kettlebell back between upper thighs like a football snap.
Drive hips forward explosively, snapping knees and glutes to float kettlebell to chest height.
Let kettlebell fall back into the hinge arc under control.
safetyNotes: Do not pull with your arms; all upward momentum comes from the violent hip snap.

alternatives.name: Dumbbell Swings
alternatives.reason: Easy substitute if kettlebells are unavailable.

alternatives.name: Assault Bike Sprint
alternatives.reason: Maximum calorie burn with low joint impact.

tips: Keep the kettlebell above knee level during the backswing.

exercises.name: Concept2 Rowing Machine Intervals
instructions: Strap feet firmly into footplates and set damper between 4 and 6.
Drive with legs first, lean back slightly with torso, then pull handle into lower sternum.
Reverse in opposite order: arms extend, torso hinges forward, knees bend.
Perform 30-second maximum effort sprints followed by 60 seconds easy recovery.
safetyNotes: Do not bend knees before arms clear them on the recovery stroke.

alternatives.name: Treadmill Incline Sprints
alternatives.reason: High intensity conditioning.

alternatives.name: Jump Rope High Knees
alternatives.reason: Zero equipment agility cardio.

tips: 60% of the rowing power comes from your legs, 20% from core swing, 20% from arm pull.
